card: CTransaction gains a templated constructor accepting generic ranges of inputs and outputs, and CTxIn constructors gain an optional script witness argument. This enables declarative construction of immutable transactions without creating and mutating intermediate CMutableTransaction objects. The PR is part of issue #36692 to simplify test transaction creation.
evidence: PR description: 'CTransaction gains a constructor that allows direct declarative construction as an alternative to building through CMutableTransaction. CTxIn's constructors gain an optional argument to pass the script witness.'
PR description: 'Part of #36692. Please view this PR in context of changes like https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36694.'
problem: Constructing an immutable CTransaction currently requires creating and modifying an intermediate CMutableTransaction, which creates boilerplate and requires mutable state when assembling test fixtures.

risk.why: A flaw in CTransaction field initialization or hash calculation could break transaction hashing or invariants across validation and consensus code.

summary: Add a templated constructor to CTransaction that accepts generic input ranges of CTxIn and CTxOut, and add an optional script witness argument to CTxIn constructors. Introduce RangeOf concept and ToVector helper in util/vector.h to construct vectors from input ranges without transferring container ownership, and update sigopcount_tests to demonstrate declarative transaction construction.
